metadata.title: OSIRIS-QAML-001: Adversarial Robustness of Staggered-DD Transmon Quantum Feature Maps vs. Classical CNNs (Preregistration Protocol v1.0)
metadata.description:
OSIRIS-QAML-001 Preregistration Protocol v1.0

This pre-registration protocol establishes an empirical hardware benchmark testing whether high-dimensional quantum feature spaces (Havlíček et al., 2019; Sen, 2024; Razavi-Far et al., 2026) protected by bipartite staggered dynamical decoupling (stag_xy8, Delta = 80 ns) confer verifiable adversarial robustness against classical norm-bounded Projected Gradient Descent (PGD-L_inf) perturbations, or whether claimed advantages collapse into transmon calibration drift (sigma_drift = 1.03 pp RMS).

Target Hardware: IBM Quantum Heron r2 (ibm_marrakesh / ibm_fez, 156-qubit heavy-hex architecture).

Five Matched Experimental Arms:

  • Arm 0 (Classical CNN Baseline): 4-layer neural network with LeakyReLU activations.
  • Arm 1 (Bare Quantum Feature Map): Unmitigated idle windows (0 ns) measuring environmental dephasing.
  • Arm 2 (Synchronous XY8 Map): Simultaneous XY8 pulses (Delta = 0 ns) refocusing single-qubit dephasing while spectator ZZ crosstalk remains active.
  • Arm 3 (Staggered XY8 Map - OSIRIS): Bipartite sublattice staggered XY8 pulses (Delta = 80 ns) suppressing both single-qubit dephasing and multi-qubit spectator ZZ crosstalk.
  • Arm 4 (Identical A/A Drift Control): Independent physical realization of Arm 3 to quantify real-time hardware calibration drift.

Statistical Power Floor: N >= 33,500 shots per basis per arm (33 randomized blocks x 1,024 shots) resolving minimum true delta = 0.50 pp at 2-sigma with 95% confidence.

Baseline Noisy-Aer Simulation: Gate 0 pre-flight simulation verified clean encoding capacity (Arm 3 clean accuracy = 96.00%), adversarial advantage over classical CNN under PGD at eps = 0.05 (Delta = +60.00 pp), and staggered crosstalk advantage over synchronous DD (Delta = +2.00 pp).
